keyFindings.description: The merge took `#2179`'s second database kind but left a Postgres-only premise in two shared launch paths, so a `cloudsql-iam` deployment with no provider keys cannot boot. `launcher.go:407-409` passes `--provider-env-dir ProvidersDir` unconditionally, with the comment 'Every pod mounts the providers Secret — it holds the session database's URL at least — so the shim is always told the directory to read it from', and `probe.go:1188-1192` does the same with 'the session database's URL key is required, so the Secret is never absent'. Both premises were true before the merge and are false after it: `providers()` returns no volume and no mount when `mountsProviders()` is false (`manifest.go:576`, `:595-598`), and `mountsProviders()` is `len(providerKeys) > 0 || len(providersSecrets) > 0 || sessionDSNKey != ""` — all three empty under `cloudsql-iam` with the model route on a projected token, which `docs/kubernetes.md` describes as that kind's point. The directory is then absent and both consumers refuse it: `internal/shim/config.go:69-73` returns `--provider-env-dir %s is unreadable`, and `cmd/legion/probe_image.go` exits non-zero before any probe runs, so the daemon's boot image probe fails rather than the pod. `mountsProviders()` already exists and is the guard both sites want. Found independently by both thermonuclear agents and verified here at the head; no deployment runs `cloudsql-iam` yet, so the path is reachable by configuration rather than in production today.

The hardened exporter's refusals are swallowed, so the proof can lose its evidence and still pass. `collect_transcripts` runs `session_copy … || note "the pods' sessions could not be copied …"`, and a `note` is not a failure: it does not append to `teardown_failed`, which is what `:2588-2589` reads to print `FAIL`, and the teardown then removes the session database's container, after which the sessions are unrecoverable. The round-4 hardening is what makes this reachable: the exporter now *refuses* a colliding pair of keys, an over-long name and the other shapes it rejects, where before it would have written them. Two keys whose derived names collide — an agent in a pod can write both, since every role container holds the session DSN — therefore destroy the whole transcript export of the run and leave a green exit. The collector's own directory names are unreserved too, so a key deriving to `controller` obstructs the operator controller's copy. Make a collection failure part of the teardown verdict before the database is destroyed, and reserve the collector's names. Read from the source; not executed.

'Postgres is the only store' survives outside the manual in five texts, three of them read by operators rather than by maintainers. The published site page says `session_store` must be `postgres`: it is the only store this runtime has (`:259`), that both keys are required (`:19`), and that the `runtime.kubernetes` block must name `session_store: postgres` and `session_dsn_secret` (`:507`). `deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example:70` — the file an operator copies — marks `session_store: postgres` as required. `scripts/e2e/README.md:16` calls `postgres` the only store the daemon loads, and `AGENTS.md:71` the same. The merged rule is that the store must keep sessions in a database: `postgres` or `cloudsql-iam`, with `pvc` and an omitted key refused. `docs/kubernetes.md` itself is correct, which is what makes these five the survivors.
The comment names `Options.SessionDSNKey` as the field the deployment's session database is named by; the merge replaced it with the store value, and the field is gone.

Prose still teaching the removed model, now in more places than round 4 named, because the merge added its own. Confirmed at this head: `podkind.go:73-75` ('the issue's own volume, which its Sandbox owns'); `cleanup.go:70-75` (Sandbox-owned PVC given as the general deletion invariant); `manifest_test.go:659-661` (logs, browser profiles and plugin generations 'outlive the pod'); `scripts/e2e/README.md:1477` (the review pair reads the issue volume, where `stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:1065-1071` reads the database); `relaunch_test.go:652-655` (the init container receives the session's location on the volume). The pair also names `manifest.go:755-759` and `:766-784`, `sandbox.go:1028-1033`, `lifecycle_test.go:290-295`, `manifest_test.go:820-825` and `stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3475-3476` (claims selected by labels a pod-owned ephemeral claim does not carry), and three texts the merge made stale in the other direction — `live_operator_test.go:141-143`, `stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3118-3120` and `api/version.go:319-320` call `postgres` the only or mandatory store — plus `docs/kubernetes.md:918-920`, which still says `legion sessions mark-lost` is unchanged while the same runbook records its removal at `:1011-1013`. I verified the five named; the rest are the pair's reading.

notAFinding.redLanes: `broker-multiprocess` and `envoy-go` are `failure` at the code head, and neither is this change's. Both fail on one compile error — `cmd/broker/service_account_scope_test.go:50` and `service_accounts_test.go:46` call `startBroker` in the pre-#2162 form against the `brokerOptions` signature — and I reproduced it in the workspace with `go vet ./...` in `packages/envoy`. The branch touches no file under `packages/envoy`: main itself landed the broken combination (#2162's signature with #2185's tests) and fixed it in #2194, which is `main@origin`'s tip `f9d5eabb`. The branch head's copies of those two files differ from main's precisely because main moved; `main_test.go` is byte-identical. Neither lane is in the base's required set. The forward merge the branch needs anyway — it is 40 behind — clears both.

roundFourVerification.note: Every round-4 finding is fixed; I verified each at the head rather than from its report.
verified: The head is MERGEABLE; the conflict against main is resolved.

The exporter no longer treats a key as a path: the name is derived under LC_ALL=C, empty/./../collisions are refused rather than sanitised, the resolved destination is asserted inside the directory before any write, and the listing returns hex so a newline-bearing key cannot arrive as two keys (stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:976-1015). The swallowed-refusal finding above is new and is a consequence of that hardening, not a return of the traversal.
scripts/e2e/README.md:965 reads OMP_SESSION_STORAGE=sql with its DSN pointer, and :967 says the throwaway pod's own disk goes with its pod.
The E2E (implementer) line cites a commit permalink that answers 200, not a branch path retro deletes.
sandboxObject defaults to the pod-owned disk, withoutVolume is gone, and three migration sites opt in with withSupersededDisk (rig_test.go:899-932).
The census and the body state the merged rule: the store must keep sessions in a database, pvc and an omitted key refused, neither demanded to be postgres.
